roster.name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
roster.pitch: Third-term President steering a neutral nation toward the Allies.
roster.reach: The Navy, the radio, and what Congress will pass.

dossier.bio: Franklin Delano Roosevelt, thirty-second President of the United States, won an unprecedented third term in November 1940. A former Assistant Secretary of the Navy and Governor of New York, he was struck by polio in 1921 and governs from a wheelchair the public rarely sees. He carried the country through the Depression with the New Deal, and now steers a neutral nation toward Britain: destroyers for bases in 1940, Lend-Lease in March 1941, the Atlantic Charter with Churchill in August. He leads by radio, by press conference and by keeping his own counsel, and he must still carry a Congress that renewed the draft by a single vote.
dossier.arena: Your arena is Washington and the western Atlantic. The Navy escorts convoys as far as Iceland on your order; Congress decides whether merchant ships may be armed and sail into the war zones; and the country is not yet sure it wants a war. What you say on the radio moves opinion. What you ask of Congress has to pass both Houses.
history: Ordered the Navy to shoot on sight at Axis raiders after the Greer incident, in a radio talk on 11 September 1941.
Asked Congress to arm merchant ships and let them sail to Britain; the Neutrality Act was revised in November 1941.
Made the Soviet Union eligible for Lend-Lease on 7 November 1941.
Asked Congress for war on Japan on 8 December 1941, the day after Pearl Harbor.
dossier.quote: When you see a rattlesnake poised to strike, you do not wait until he has struck before you crush him.
dossier.source: Fireside chat on the Greer incident, 11 September 1941
dossier.fact: He is the only President elected to a third term.

roster.name: Winston Churchill
roster.pitch: Prime Minister holding on until America comes in.
roster.reach: The War Cabinet, the Chiefs of Staff, and cables to Roosevelt.

dossier.bio: Winston Spencer Churchill became Prime Minister in May 1940, as France fell, and leads a coalition government from Downing Street and the Cabinet War Rooms. A soldier, war correspondent and writer before he was a politician, he was First Lord of the Admiralty in both wars and spent the 1930s warning against German rearmament. Britain stood without a major ally from the summer of 1940; since June 1941 the Soviet Union fights beside it, and it lives on American supplies carried across an Atlantic where the U-boats hunt. His tools are the War Cabinet, the Chiefs of Staff, the House of Commons, and a private correspondence with Roosevelt that he signs "Former Naval Person".
dossier.arena: Your arena is the Atlantic lifeline and the House of Commons. The Home Fleet and the escorts decide whether the convoys reach Britain; the Commons expects them covered; and every cable to Washington asks for a little more than America has yet agreed to give.
history: Agreed the Atlantic Charter with Roosevelt at Placentia Bay in August 1941.
Sent the first Arctic convoy of aid to the Soviet Union in August 1941.
Opened Operation Crusader to relieve Tobruk on 18 November 1941.
Crossed to Washington after Pearl Harbor to plan the war with Roosevelt.
dossier.quote: Give us the tools, and we will finish the job.
dossier.fact: He sat in the House of Commons for the first time in 1901.

roster.name: Burton K. Wheeler
roster.pitch: The Senate's loudest voice for staying out of the war.
roster.reach: His vote, his speeches, and the America First rallies.

setting.situation: September 1941. Britain has fought Germany for two years, and since June the Soviet Union fights too. The United States is neutral in law: it lends and leases Britain the means of war, and its Navy escorts convoys as far as Iceland, where the U-boats wait.
sides: Those who would bring America into the war: the President's men, and Britain
Those who would keep America out: Wheeler, America First and much of Congress
Germany, whose U-boats make the choice harder every week
crawl: It is September 1941. For two years Britain has fought Germany, alone for much of that time. Since June the Soviet Union has fought too, and it is falling back.

Across the Atlantic, the United States is neutral in law and not in fact. American ships carry Lend-Lease to Britain, American destroyers escort the convoys as far as Iceland, and German U-boats wait beyond.
In Washington and London, a few people will decide how long that can last. One of them is you.
facts: The Neutrality Act still bars American merchant ships from the war zones.
The House renewed the draft by one vote, 203 to 202, on 12 August 1941.
American troops landed in Iceland in July 1941.
Roosevelt and Churchill met at Placentia Bay in August 1941.

dates.what: USS Greer and U-652 exchange fire south of Iceland.
Congress can take up the arming of merchant ships.
